thesis: Q2 2026 earnings showed record revenue (+164% YoY) on surging indium phosphide substrate demand for AI-datacenter optics, with raised Q3 guidance and a >$100M backlog reinforced by multiyear supply deals with Coherent and Lumentum. The main counter-case is AXTI's dependence on Chinese export permits, which caused a guidance miss in Q4 2025, but permit issuance has eased since Q1 2026 and current backlog growth suggests this isn't currently binding. A pending securities class action was dismissed with leave to amend in July 2026, with no new scheduled hearing.
invalidation: A renewed China export-permit freeze that stalls InP/GaAs shipments, or a guidance miss versus the ~$66M Q3 revenue target, would invalidate this.

thesis: Record Q2 2026 results (revenue +257% YoY, 76% operating margin) on HBM4 mass production and AI-memory demand from Nvidia, AMD, Meta and Microsoft support continued strength, reinforced by long-term supply agreements with roughly ten customers. The main counter-case is that HBM/DRAM pricing is historically cyclical and a sequential ASP decline has previously pulled the stock down 15-25%, but current demand signals for Blackwell/Rubin-generation chips show no sign of that reversal yet.
invalidation: A sequential decline in HBM ASP/pricing, or a guidance cut tied to HBM4 yields/capacity, would invalidate this.

thesis: Record Q2 FY2027 revenue (+37% YoY) and a second consecutive guidance raise, driven by an expanded Google TPU-ecosystem custom-silicon partnership and new AI infrastructure products, support the move. Elevated valuation (~73x trailing earnings) and a run of insider selling with no offsetting buys are real cautions, and an Oct 6 Investor Day is a near-term event that could disappoint against high expectations, which keeps this from a higher-conviction read.
invalidation: A disappointing Investor Day (Oct 6) on margin/TAM guidance, or loss of a major hyperscaler custom-silicon design win, would invalidate this.

thesis: Q2 FY2027 results (revenue +106% YoY, raised Q3 guide) and the Hugging Face acquisition support continued fundamental strength, but nothing this cycle is a fresh disclosed catalyst beyond what was already priced in by late August. A September 14 selloff tied to sector-wide AI-capex-slowdown commentary appears to be sentiment rather than a confirmed hyperscaler budget cut, and China export-policy uncertainty remains an unresolved, ongoing risk rather than a new deterioration.
invalidation: Confirmed hyperscaler capex cuts (not just commentary) or a further tightening of China export policy that hits guidance would invalidate this.

thesis: AAPL is trading near its 52-week high on the iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max launch (Sept 18) and early positive purchase-intent survey data, reinforced by a ninth consecutive earnings beat and a string of analyst price-target increases. This reads as still-anticipatory ahead of confirmed holiday-quarter sell-through data, and a Q3 report already showed China and Services softness alongside a rich valuation, so it doesn't yet clear the bar for a confirmed, already-realized catalyst.
invalidation: iPhone 18 sell-through data (holiday quarter) coming in below the current bullish purchase-intent surveys, or a fresh China/Services deterioration, would invalidate this.

thesis: Q2 2026 results showed Starlink subscriber growth of 2x YoY on $7.8B revenue (+92%), reinforced by a $946M NASA crewed-flight contract expansion disclosed Sept 18. The main counter-case is that SpaceX's bonds trade like junk despite investment-grade ratings and S&P projects negative free cash flow through 2029 as Starlink profits fund cash-burning Space/AI units, which alongside an unresolved Starship Flight 14 launch (Sept 28) argues for a moderate rather than high-conviction read.
invalidation: A Starship Flight 14 (Sept 28) failure with material program setback, or a miss versus the ~$100B annualized revenue run-rate guide, would invalidate this.

thesis: Q2 FY2027 results beat sharply (revenue +58% YoY, EPS +203%) on record AI-server orders and a record $95B backlog, prompting a full-year guidance raise (revenue to ~$192B, EPS to $25.50) and a wave of analyst price-target increases. AI-server gross margins are structurally thinner than the legacy mix, a known and already-disclosed risk, but a small pending Irish court case over disputed server pricing (adjourned to December 2026) keeps this at a lower-conviction read despite the strength of the core catalyst.
invalidation: A miss on the raised FY2027 guidance (revenue ~$192B, EPS $25.50) or a further deterioration in AI-server gross margins beyond current expectations would invalidate this.

thesis: Today's move to a fresh 52-week high and volume spike is largely explained by a broad, sector-wide semiconductor rally tied to optimism around this week's Trump-Xi summit, not a fresh AMD-specific disclosure — the underlying chip-supply deals with Meta, OpenAI, Oracle and Anthropic are real but predate this move by weeks to months. Consensus analyst price targets (~$613-616) are already roughly in line with today's price, suggesting limited support for chasing the extended move here.
invalidation: A pullback to a level meaningfully below current consensus price targets (~$613-616), or a fresh AMD-specific fundamental catalyst (rather than sector-wide sentiment), would revisit this avoid call.

thesis: WBD's new 52-week high and ~12.5x volume spike reflect a same-day settlement between Paramount Skydance and a 12-state AG coalition that clears the last major legal obstacle to closing Paramount's ~$31/share all-cash acquisition of WBD, not organic business strength. With the current price only about $0.20 below the deal price, this is arbitrage spread convergence with capped upside, not a fresh momentum catalyst worth a new entry.
invalidation: A collapse of the Paramount deal (e.g. a court blocking final closing, or a material adverse event before close) would remove the arb-driven price support entirely; a completed close at $31/share would also end the trade opportunity by removing the spread.
